findings.summary: Lease claim path can replace an active unexpired claim without CAS/expiry fencing.
findings.details: S06-T01 requires claim-by-compare-and-set with leaseGeneration, opaque token, owner, expiry, attempt, heartbeat, reclaim, and stale-worker fencing. The core startSourceJob reducer increments leaseGeneration for any non-accepted row and enqueueSourceJobHandler calls it for an existing row that has no workId, without checking that an existing lease has expired. A duplicate enqueue after claim but before workId patch can therefore steal the active lease instead of preserving the prior claim or waiting for expiry/reclaim, and no heartbeat Confect function is exposed to maintain the current token.
evidence: packages/convex/confect/jobs/jobState.ts:184-217 startSourceJob only checks acceptedEffectKey and does not require queued/retry_wait or expired status before issuing a new leaseGeneration/token.

packages/convex/confect/jobs/workpool.ts:182-211 finds an existing row with no workId and immediately calls startSourceJob; it only returns existing.workId when workId is already present or claim returns Left.
packages/convex/confect/jobs/leases.ts:14-30 defines heartbeatLease, but packages/convex/confect/jobs/workpool.spec.ts:11-31 registers no heartbeat function.

findings.summary: Declared failure contract is not surfaced through registered Confect/Convex functions.
findings.details: The task requires typed errors and reachable retry/permanent/max-attempt/cancel/revoke/supersede paths. The spec registers enqueue/status/background/onComplete only, with no expected-error declarations, while failure and reclaim handlers are exported as plain helper functions but not wired into the Confect group. The registered background action always succeeds with null and onComplete only performs the success path, so workpool action failures cannot persist the declared retry_wait/dead_letter states or surface the declared typed errors through the API contract.
